column1: # What each install matrix cell and facet is expected to do, read by
# install/matrix-gate.sh. Tab separated: cell, facet, pass|fail|untested, note.
# This is the record of what the installed product does on each kind of machine.
# Any other result fails the gate, in both directions: a cell that starts failing
# is a regression, and a cell that starts passing is a fix that belongs in the
# same change as its new expectation. "untested" means the facet was not
# exercised, and it is never accepted in place of "pass".
# Two rules live in install/matrix-gate.sh instead of here and cannot be edited
# out of this file: the noexec-tmp cells must pass every facet, because that is
# the failure that cost a first customer; and the arm64 cells may come back
# untested on a runner with no emulator, reported as untested and never as a pass.
# Measured against the published v0.1.7 assets on 2026-10-01, 8 core Debian host,
# docker 29.6.2. Two groups of rows are what a correct release does rather than
# what v0.1.7 does, and are marked OPEN DEFECT. Until the release under test
# carries those fixes this gate is red, and that is the whole point of it.
# --- machines that have everything the installer needs -----------------------
# install.sh is a bash script and the documented command pipes it into bash, so a
# machine with no bash cannot install. That is a prerequisite, stated in the
# README, and the facets behind it are unreachable rather than broken.

column4: no bash: install.sh is a bash script, which the README names as a prerequisite

column1: # OPEN DEFECT. The musl build is linked against libstdc++ and libgcc_s, which
# Alpine does not install by default, so a stock Alpine machine installs the
# archive and gets a binary that cannot start: "Error loading shared library
# libstdc++.so.6". alpine-libstdcpp below is the control -- the same archive on
# the same image with libstdc++ added passes every facet -- so the fix is either
# to link statically or to say in the installer which packages musl needs.

column4: OPEN DEFECT: musl build needs libstdc++ and libgcc_s, absent from stock Alpine

column1: # The control for the two above: musl works, the missing C++ runtime is the bug.
# A noexec /tmp, the shared and cPanel hosting default. The install, the PATH,
# --version, doctor, the sign in and the billing all report success and the
# program cannot start, because the native render library is unpacked into the
# temporary directory and then refused a mapping. Required to pass: the gate
# enforces these three cells itself, whatever this file says.
# v0.1.7 fails the tui facet here with
#   Failed to initialize OpenTUI render library: ... failed to map segment
# which is verbatim what the two users saw. 0.1.8 restarts itself with TMPDIR
# pointing at a directory that can execute, which is what noexec-tmp-tmpdir

column4: REQUIRED: the failure that cost a first customer
REQUIRED: the documented way out of a noexec /tmp must keep working

column1: # --- machines the installer is right to refuse --------------------------------
# These failures are the installer saying what is missing and stopping, which is
# the correct behaviour. The detail is asserted by install/test-install.sh; what
# this file records is that the refusal still happens and still happens early.
# Since 0.1.10 the installer does not stop on a temporary folder that is too
# small: it unpacks in ~/.rafikicode/tmp and says so, and the binary replaces
# the same folder for itself at every start. --version prints the version and
# nothing else on standard output there; the line about the folder is kept for

column4: falls back to ~/.rafikicode/tmp for the download
the version alone on standard output
